'''Classic''' is a constructed format on [[GEMP]] (code <code>classic</code>). Its card pool is the same as [[Open]], with three banned icons.<ref name="gemp" /> [[Scott Lingrell]] ran a Classic Format playtest at [[DecipherCon 2002]].<ref name="dcon2002" /> The Players Committee made Classic an official format for all sanctioned events on 31 March 2003.<ref name="pc-classic03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030824053912/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/classicnews03312003.htm Classic Format Contest Results are In!], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 24 August 2003.</ref>

* '''Designed by:''' [[Scott Lingrell]]<ref name="dcon2002" />
* '''Type:''' constructed
* '''GEMP:''' ''Classic'' (<code>classic</code>)

The card pool is Decipher-printed set ids 1&ndash;14 ([[Premiere]] through [[Theed Palace]]) and premium ids 101&ndash;112. It also includes current Virtual Sets 0&ndash;27 (ids 200&ndash;227) and the Virtual Premium Set (id 301). Cards with the Defensive Shield, Episode I or Maintenance icon are banned.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="sets" />

== Deck size ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Default deck size on [[GEMP]]
| 60 cards
|}
The GEMP format definition sets no deck size, so GEMP uses its default of 60 cards.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="lib-ec48dc19" />

== Players Committee definition ==
The Players Committee ''Alternate Format Tournament Guide'' (revised September 2015) lists Classic among its closed environment formats. Players build constructed decks from any Decipher cards or Virtual Cards (Legacy or Standard, depending on the event), except:<ref name="afg" />
* any card, including Defensive Shields, with an Episode I icon. The guide notes that ''Desperate Times'' has been clarified not to have the Episode I icon, so it is legal.
* any maintenance card, for example ''Blizzard 4'' or ''Lando Calrissian, Scoundrel''.
The GEMP definition also bans every card with the Defensive Shield icon.<ref name="gemp" />

== Players Committee history ==
The first Classic Format event was a non-sanctioned playtest tournament at [[DecipherCon 2002]] on Friday 1 November 2002, run by [[Scott Lingrell]] to gauge players' acceptance of the format; [[Drew Scott]] won it and $35.<ref name="pc-dconwrap">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030424052656/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/dconwrapup.htm DecipherCon 2002], Andrew Howard (Tournament Support Advocate), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 24 April 2003.</ref> Over the winter the Players Committee ran a Winter Classic Contest for tournament directors and players. On 31 March 2003 it announced the winners (1st [[Jacob Taylor]] of San Marcos, Texas; 2nd [[Christian Kriesel]] of Madison, Wisconsin; 3rd [[David Kangas]] of Brush Prairie, Washington) and that, "effective immediately, Classic Format will be considered an official format for all sanctioned events", including the Championship Circuit, with a Classic Format Subcommittee reviewing the ban list; Virtual Set 5 was to include two alternative Starting Effects aimed at Classic.<ref name="pc-classic03" /> The first official ban list (31 March 2003) banned all cards with an Episode 1 icon, all cards with a maintenance cost, all "insert" cards and Watch Your Step / This Place Can Be A Little Rough.<ref name="pc-classicban">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030413134208/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Resources/classicbanlist.htm SWCCG Classic Format Ban List], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 13 April 2003.</ref>

In 2003 several Championship Circuit events were played in Classic: the California, Ohio and Virginia State Championships and the United Kingdom National Championship,<ref name="pc-us03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040622065452/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/usevents.htm State Championships (US Events)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 22 June 2004.</ref><ref name="pc-intl03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040621085705/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/intlevents.htm Nationals and Provincials (International Events)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 21 June 2004.</ref> a Classic Format Open Qualifier in Vancouver, Washington, on 2 August 2003,<ref name="pc-waclassic">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030809112718/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/WAclassicopen06122003.htm Classic Format Open Qualifier, Vancouver, WA], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 9 August 2003.</ref> and one of the two Day 1 qualifiers of the [[2003 World Championship]].<ref name="pc-wc03sched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040620165803/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/worldchamps06122003.htm SWCCG World Championships Coming to Atlanta!], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 20 June 2004.</ref>

== Variants on GEMP ==
* [[Classic (no v-cards)]] (<code>classic_no_virtual</code>) &mdash; the same banned icons, Decipher cards only.<ref name="gemp" />
* [[Classic (no v-cards) (Modified)]] (<code>classic_no_virtual_m</code>) &mdash; Decipher cards only, with 14 Defensive Shields allowed.<ref name="gemp" />
